transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-07-22
Time: 09:00 AM PT - 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Nair, Marcus Li (Redwood) / Sarah Thompson, Daniel Park, Leah Martinez, Rita Gomez (Bluehaven)

Summary: Quick kickoff to align on onboarding path for Bluehaven Clinic. High-level goals: integrate Redwood for clinical summarization and patient triage automation, pilot on dedicated capacity with option to move to private deployment if needed for compliance.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Alex from Redwood here, I'm the AE on this account. Quick intros?
[00:05] Sarah Thompson: Hi, Sarah, head of ML at Bluehaven. We're excited to get started.
[00:07] Daniel Park: Daniel, CTO. I will own infra and security signoffs.
[00:09] Leah Martinez: Leah, platform eng. I'll be hands-on for VPC and networking.
[00:11] Rita Gomez: Rita, compliance. I'll work through SOC2 and data residency items.
[00:13] Priya Nair: Priya, SE at Redwood, I'll be your technical lead for the pilot.
[00:15] Marcus Li: Marcus, CSM, I'll run the onboarding project plan and success milestones.

[00:20] Alex Chen: Great. To start, can you remind us of the core business problem and what success looks like at the end of the pilot?
[00:24] Sarah Thompson: Yeah, so we're building an assistant to auto-summarize clinician notes and a triage assistant for inbound patient messages. Success for us is a 90%+ accuracy on summaries in the validation set, under 300ms median latency for short prompts in production and clear data isolation for PHI.
[00:36] Daniel Park: And from infra perspective, we need audit logs and KMS integration for keys. We also have a requirement that any PHI processing happens in a private VPC or an on-prem option.
[00:44] Priya Nair: Got it. Those are pretty typical enterprise asks. For latency under 300ms, we usually recommend Redwood Dedicated for the pilot so we can guarantee throughput, and if you want full control for PHI, Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) is the longer-term option. We'll scope both.
[00:58] Leah Martinez: When you say Dedicated can guarantee latency, what are the typical SLOs? Also what's the difference operationally for us between Dedicated and Private?
[01:04] Priya Nair: Dedicated is isolated GPU pools in our infra with predictable capacity and an SLA. Private is where the control plane is customer's VPC or we deploy a private stack on-prem — more work up front but gives you key management and full network control. For Dedicated we handle the GPU fabric and infra, you get predictable latency; for Private you own more of the infra but get the isolation you asked about.
[01:20] Sarah Thompson: Okay. For compliance, we definitely need KMS integration and audit logs. Rita, anything else?
[01:24] Rita Gomez: SOC2 Type II evidence will be needed. Also we need to confirm data retention policies and whether Redwood supports in-transit and at-rest encryption with customer KMS. Role-based access and SSO are important too.
[01:33] Marcus Li: We have a security pack we usually send — it contains SOC2 reports, ISO docs, and the KMS/SSO integration guides. I'll circulate that after the call.
[01:41] Alex Chen: Next, let's talk pilot scope and timeline. Our suggested approach: 2-week discovery, 4-week pilot where we run parallel traffic routing, and a final evaluation. Thoughts?
[01:49] Daniel Park: Sounds reasonable. Two weeks for discovery will let us gather sample workloads and confirm infra. Is there a recommended minimal data set for the validation?
[01:56] Priya Nair: Typically we ask for ~5k representative notes for model evals and a synthetic stream to test throughput. We can provide a template.
[02:04] Leah Martinez: On the network side, we'll need details on VPC peering, IP ranges, and firewall rules. We also have to check with our security team about inbound connections.
[02:12] Priya Nair: For Dedicated we can work with a set of egress IPs; for Private we will need a peering setup or a customer-hosted control plane. We'll send a network checklist.
[02:20] Sarah Thompson: Any constraints around model versions or quantization? We have a custom fine-tuned model for summaries.
[02:26] Priya Nair: We can host fine-tuned model artifacts in Dedicated or Private. For hosted variants we have restrictions around customer model uploads, so Dedicated or Private is safer for custom models. We support various quantization profiles; Priya: the SE explains a little garble here — we sometimes say quantize pro-files and kernel choices will depend on your sequence length.
[02:46] Daniel Park: Good. On logging, can you retain per-request logs for 180 days? We may need them for audit.
[02:52] Marcus Li: We have configurable retention. Longer retention is an add-on — we'll include options in the SOW.
[02:58] Rita Gomez: And do you provide redaction or automated PHI masking? We prefer to avoid sending raw PHI where possible.
[03:04] Priya Nair: We have client-side SDK hooks for redaction, and we can also recommend pre-processing patterns. We do not recommend sending raw PHI to hosted endpoints without proper controls — that's why Private is attractive.
[03:14] Alex Chen: Let's surface the stakeholders and approvals: Daniel will own infra signoff, Rita will own compliance signoff, Sarah owns ML success criteria, and Leah will own integration. Any additions?
[03:22] Sarah Thompson: That's correct. Marcus will run the onboarding plan.
[03:24] Marcus Li: I'll create a shared timeline with milestones and dependencies and invite the stakeholders.
[03:29] Alex Chen: On commercials, we'll propose a pilot pricing for Dedicated reserved capacity and options to convert to Private. I'll send a draft SOW.
[03:36] Daniel Park: We will need procurement details for billing contact. Marcus, can you capture that?
[03:39] Marcus Li: Yes, I'll send the billing form.
[03:41] Alex Chen: Any blockers we should know about today?
[03:43] Leah Martinez: We need to scope network approvals; our security team will require a short questionnaire.
[03:47] Rita Gomez: Also we'd like to review the SOC2 report and KMS integration doc.
[03:50] Priya Nair: We'll share the security pack and a network checklist as part of the next steps.
[03:54] Alex Chen: Great — next steps recap: Redwood sends onboarding checklist, security pack, draft SOW, trial access. Bluehaven sends sample dataset, network diagram, and compliance questions. We'll target first technical deep-dive next Wednesday.
[04:05] Sarah Thompson: Works for us.
[04:06] Daniel Park: Agree.
[04:07] Leah Martinez: Sounds good.
[04:08] Rita Gomez: Fine.
[04:09] Priya Nair: Before we wrap, any technical concerns around latency or batch size?
[04:13] Sarah Thompson: Our typical median prompt is 150 tokens; peak concurrency could be 40 qps initially. We need guidance on batching vs single-shot to hit 300ms.
[04:21] Priya Nair: For 150-token prompts at 40 qps, Dedicated with optimized batching and KV cache should hit your latency target — we'll run a perf estimate. If you need consistent sub-300ms at peak, we may recommend reserving additional burst capacity.
[04:33] Alex Chen: Ok, I'll leave Priya and Leah to schedule the architecture deep-dive. Marcus will follow up with docs and trial access. Thanks everyone.
[04:39] End of recording.

Notes on transcription quality: Mild stutters and occasional mis-hearings of product names (e.g., "quantize profiles" as "quantize pro-files"). Speaker labels are accurate.
